paragraphs.text: Export generated text as a real Word .docx from any DeepSeek Harness session — zero dependencies.
# dsh-docx-export
**English** | 中文
Export generated text as a **real Word document** (`.docx`) from any DeepSeek Harness session — not
a renamed Markdown file, but a proper OOXML package with native heading styles, multilevel lists, ta
bles, code blocks, quotes, hyperlinks, embedded pictures, a table-of-contents field and a page-numbe
red footer. Word, WPS, LibreOffice and Google Docs all open it as-is.
Zero runtime dependencies (only Node's built-in `zlib`), no `@deepseek-ai/*` imports, so it survives
harness version drift. It installs as a bundle and mounts on the next start.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Features
| Markdown you write | What lands in Word |

| `# Title` … `###### Title` | Heading 1–6 styles (template-friendly, TOC-ready) |
| Paragraphs, `**
bold**`, `*italic*`, `~~strike~~`, `` `code` `` | Real character formatting, CJK `w:eastAsia` fonts

included |
| `- item` / `1. step`, nested by indentation | True multilevel bullet and numbered lists

(`numbering.xml`) |
| `- [x] done` / `- [ ] todo` | ☑ / ☐ checklist items |
| `

The suite ships its own ZIP central-directory reader with CRC verification, an XML well-formedness c
hecker and a miniature PNG encoder, so there are no dev dependencies either.
## Publishing and sharing

- Add the GitHub topic **`dsh-plugin`** so discovery sweeps pick the repository up.
- Submit it to t
he community catalog with a PR to `data/plugins.json` in dshworks/awesome-dsh-plugins (fields: that

repo's `data/schema.json`).
- Publish to npm with `npm publish`, after which `dsh plugin --profile <

profile> add dsh-docx-export` installs it from the registry.
- Details: docs/PUBLISHING.md.
## Compatibility

- Node ≥ 20 (`node:zlib`, ESM).
- Any DSH from 0.1.7 on: the plugin declares no `@deepseek-ai/*` pee
r dependencies and imports no host package — it uses the runtime's raw JSON-Schema tool-registration

path.
- Measured on DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 (Windows desktop): install → mount → generate → structural check
→ LibreOffice render.
